summary:
An Allwork.Space republication (originally Fortune, via Reuters Connect syndication) reports on Crist Kolder Associates' mid-year 2026 Volatility Report, which studied leadership at 665 Fortune 500 and S&P 500 companies. CFO turnover for full-year 2026 is projected at 18.3%, the highest since the pandemic, versus 18.2% in 2020 and 19.3% in 2019, against a 10-year historical average of 16%. Scott W. Simmons, co-managing partner at Crist Kolder, attributes the churn to expanding job demands, with some CFOs retiring and others recruited to lead turnarounds or AI initiatives.

The piece lists notable first-half Fortune 500 moves: AT&T's Pascal Desroches retiring Dec. 31 with Jennifer Biry (20-year AT&T finance veteran, ex-CFO/COO of McAfee) named deputy CFO effective July 6 and succeeding him Jan. 1, 2027; Caterpillar's Andrew Bonfield retiring Oct. 1 after eight years, with Kyle Epley taking over May 1 and Bonfield advising through transition; Oracle hiring Hilary Maxson (formerly Schneider Electric) in April, tied to Oracle's AI and cloud infrastructure buildout; Nike hiring Pfizer's David Denton on Aug. 17 amid a turnaround; and Pfizer naming Cecile Guegan interim CFO Aug. 16 while running an internal and external search.

The report, based on data through July 31, also finds newly appointed CFOs are getting younger: average CFO age is projected at 48 in 2026 versus 52 in 2025. Simmons notes average sitting CFO tenure is 4.5 years and only about 25% of new CFOs come from another sitting CFO role, suggesting companies must tap younger, less experienced talent.

The item is executive-search and finance-leadership news with no coverage of workplace technology, visitor management, desk or room booking, hybrid policy, workplace analytics, or facilities operations.
